canonical_name: Dias da Silva-Hamidoune restricted-sumset theorem family (general h-fold root versus Erdos-Heilbronn h = 2 specialization open)
category: 组合数学 / 计数组合
source_attribution: J. A. Dias da Silva and Y. O. Hamidoune; 1994 (catalog metadata crosschecked against DOI 10.1112/blms/26.2.140)
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: For a prime p, a finite subset A of the field or cyclic group of order p, and an admissible natural h, the set of sums of h pairwise distinct members of A has cardinality at least min(p, h * (|A| - h) + 1); its h = 2 case is the Erdos-Heilbronn self-sumset bound min(p, 2 * |A| - 3).
target_disposition: retain the published Dias da Silva-Hamidoune restricted-sumset family at provisional H1/M4/R4, freeze no canonical proposition, and require primary-source review plus explicit general-h/h=2 and THM-M-0934 ownership resolution
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies only 'proof of the Erdos-Heilbronn conjecture', not a proposition. Accessible scholarly sources call either the general h-fold restricted-sumset bound or its h = 2 specialization the Dias da Silva-Hamidoune theorem, while the primary 1994 article text and internal theorem locator were not accessible. The catalog omits the selected root, field/group and set encoding, binder order, h range, nonemptiness, pairwise-distinct representation, arithmetic convention, boundary cases, and relationship to THM-M-0934. Selecting a canonical target now would invent, broaden, narrow, or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Expected finite subsets of F_p or ZMod p with p prime, a natural restricted-sum cardinal h, and natural cardinality bounds. Exact universe serialization, set/finset representation, decidable equality, field/group transport, coercions, and typeclass context remain open.
conclusion: Open: the general fixed-cardinality restricted subset-sum lower bound, only its h = 2 unequal-pair specialization, or a source-approved package with a checked specialization transport.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before target selection; primality, empty and singleton sets, h = 0, 1, 2, and |A|, h > |A|, natural subtraction, the saturation branch, and duplicate/order conventions must be explicitly resolved and mutation-tested.
